subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist + next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist + next steps

Hi Amy,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Below is a concise recap and a recommended shortlist of model options we think are the best fit for the ACME customer support summarization + routing use case you showed: short documents (1-3 paragraphs), high volume (bursting), and strict latency targets (<300ms p50).

Quick recap / priorities you shared:
- Summaries must be accurate for regulatory QA (no hallucinations)
- p50 latency target: 200-300ms; some peak traffic spikes
- Cost sensitivity: target < $0.003/token equivalent for production
- Need an eval harness to track quality regressions over time

Recommended model shortlist (tradeoffs: cost / latency / quality):
1) RW-Large-Quant (base-8 quantized) — Best latency/cost balance
   - Rationale: quantized variant runs on our Dedicated GPU pools, avg p50 180ms on ACME request profile, cost ~ $0.0022/token equiv; high quality on short-form summarization in our evals.
2) RW-XL-Standard (non-quantized) — Highest quality, higher cost
   - Rationale: better at nuanced extraction and instruction fidelity; avg p50 260ms, cost ~ $0.0045/token equiv; recommended for initial canary to measure quality delta.
3) RW-Medium-Fast (smaller model) — Lowest cost, best throughput
   - Rationale: p50 ~120ms, cost ~ $0.0011/token equiv, lower recall on edge cases; good fallback for heavy-backlog or burst handling.

Attachments: acme-model-shortlist-v1.pdf (detailed benchmarks), acme-prompt-set-v1.json (seed prompts for evals), latency-cost-benchmarks.csv (raw numbers).

Proposed next steps:
- Rishi: attach benchmark links + eval dashboards (we'll need a short prompt set from you to run the first quality pass).
- Amy / David: confirm which model to pilot (we suggest starting with RW-Large-Quant + canary RW-XL-Standard for a week).
- Set up a 30-minute follow-up next week to review initial eval results and rollout plan.

If that looks right, I can kick off a pilot request and loop in our Dedicated ops to reserve the pool for your expected burst traffic.

Best,

--
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — adding the concrete benchmark links and a quick note on eval approach below.

Summary of benchmarks (links attached in Drive):
- Short-form summarization suite (ACME seed prompts) — link: https://drive.redwood.com/s/acme/model-shortlist (see folder /benchmarks/short-summaries)
- Latency/cost sweep results for our Dedicated pool (CSV attached)

Key observations from our internal evals with ACME prompt set:
- RW-Large-Quant: precision on entity retention 96%, hallucination cases low (0.8% of samples), p50=180ms, p95=420ms for long-tail batches.
- RW-XL-Standard: precision 98.5%, hallucination ~0.4%, p50=260ms, p95=480ms.
- RW-Medium-Fast: precision 89%, hallucination 1.8%, p50=120ms, p95=300ms.

Suggested canary plan:
- Week 0: Run 1k seed prompts through all three models in parallel; collect quality metrics (precision, hallucination rate, answer stability) and token-cost estimates.
- Week 1: Canary RW-Large-Quant in production lane for 10% traffic; RW-XL-Standard for 5% (A/B for quality check). Keep RW-Medium-Fast as fallback for backlog flushes.

Files attached to this thread:
- latency-cost-benchmarks.csv (CSV with p50/p95, cost estimates per token-equivalent)
- acme-prompt-set-v1.json (50 seeded prompts we used)

If you want, I can push the initial 1k-run results to the shared Drive and flag any regression alerts in the Redwood Optimize dashboard.

--
